An Act making appropriations for the fiscal year 2024 for the maintenance of the departments, 
boards, commissions, institutions, and certain activities of the Commonwealth, for interest, 
sinking fund, and serial bond requirements, and for certain permanent improvements. 
 
 Whereas, The deferred operation of this act would tend to defeat its purpose, which is to 
which is immediately to make appropriations for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2023, and to 
make certain changes in law, each of which is immediately necessary or appropriate to effectuate 
said appropriations or for other important public purposes, therefore it is hereby declared to be an 
emergency law, necessary for the immediate preservation of the public convenience. 
 
 Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives in General Court assembled, and by the authority 
of the same, as follows: 
 
 SECTION 1. To provide for the operations of the several departments, boards, commissions and 
institutions of the commonwealth and other services of the commonwealt h and for certain permanent 
improvements and to meet certain requirements of law, the sums set forth in this act, for the several 
purposes and subject to the conditions specified, are hereby appropriated from the General Fund unless 
specifically designated otherwise, subject to the laws regulating the disbursement of public funds and the 
approval thereof for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2024. All sums appropriated under this act, including 
supplemental and deficiency budgets, shall be expended in a manne r reflecting and encouraging a policy 
of nondiscrimination and equal opportunity for members of minority groups, women and persons with a 
disability. All officials and employees of an agency, board, department, commission or division receiving 
funds under this act shall take affirmative steps to ensure equality of opportunity in the internal affairs of 
state government and in their relations with the public, including those persons and organizations doing 
2 of 2 
business with the commonwealth. Each agency, board, department, commission and division of the 
commonwealth, in spending appropriated sums and discharging its statutory responsibilities, shall adopt 
measures to ensure equal opportunity in the areas of hiring, promotion, demotion or transfer, recruitment, 
layoff or termination, rates of compensation, in -service or apprenticeship training programs and all other 
terms and conditions of employment. 
 SECTION 1A. In accordance with Articles LXIII and CVII of the Articles of Amendment to the 
Constitution of the Commonwealth and section 6D of chapter 29 of the General Laws, it is hereby 
declared that the amounts of revenue set forth in this section by sou rce for the respective funds of the 
commonwealth for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2024 are necessary and sufficient to provide the 
means to defray the appropriations and expenditures from such funds for said fiscal year as set forth and 
authorized in th is act. The comptroller shall keep a distinct account of actual receipts from each such 
source by each such fund to furnish the executive office for administration and finance and the house and 
senate committees on ways and means with quarterly statements comparing such receipts with the 
projected receipts set forth in this section, and include a full statement comparing such actual and 
projected receipts in the annual report for said fiscal year pursuant to section 12 of chapter 7A of the 
General Laws. The quarterly and annual reports shall also include detailed statements of any other 
sources of revenue for the budgeted funds in addition to those specified in this section.

Conference Committee Report 
 
a period of 6 months from the date that the income level was exceeded;

permanent housing since leaving the housing situation that they fled; (ii) 
through no fault of their own, are homeless due to fire, flood or natural 
disaster; (iii) through no fault of their own, have been subject to eviction 
from their most recent housing due to: (a) foreclosure; (b) condemnation; 
(c) conduct by a guest or former household member who is not part of the 
household seeking emergency shelter and over whose conduct the 
remaining household members had no control; or (d) nonpayment of rent 
caused by a documented medical condition or diagnosed disability or 
caused by a documented loss of income within the last 12 months directly 
as a result of a c hange in household composition or a loss of income

the family remain in the housing situation; provided further, that temporary 
emergency assistance shall be provided to families who, on the date of

emergency assistance under the preceding proviso; (2) the number of 
families entering the emergency assistance system after having already 
stayed in a place not meant for human habitation; (3) the number of 
families entering the emergency assistance system hav ing stayed in a 
place not meant for human habitation after having requested services

received a written denial of their request for services prior to staying in a

SECTION 2B. 
 
SECTION 2B. Notwithstanding any general or special law to the contrary, the agencies listed in this section 
may expend the amounts listed in this section for the provision of services to agencies listed in section 2. 
All expenditures made under this section shall be accompanied by a corresponding transfer of funds fr om 
an account listed in said section 2 to the Intragovernmental Service Fund established in section 2Q of 
chapter 29 of the General Laws. All revenues and other inflows shall be based on rates published by the 
seller agency that are developed in accordance with cost principles established by the United States Office 
of Management and Budget Circular A-87, Cost Principles for State, Local and Indian Tribal Governments. 
All rates shall be published within 30 days after the effective date of this section. No e xpenditures shall be 
made from the Intragovernmental Service Fund which would cause that fund to be in deficit at the close of 
fiscal year 2024. All authorizations in this section shall be charged to the Intragovernmental Service Fund 
 Fiscal Year 2024 Budget 
 
and shall not be subj ect to section 5D of said chapter 29. Any balance remaining in that fund at the close 
of fiscal year 2024 shall be transferred to the General Fund.

SECTION 2E. 
 
SECTION 2E. The sums set forth in this section are hereby appropriated for transfer from the General Fund 
to the trust funds named within each item unless specifically designated otherwise in this section, for the 
purposes and subject to the conditions specified in this section and subject to the laws regulating the 
disbursement of public funds for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2024. Items in this section shall not be 
subject to allotment under section 9B of chapter 29 of the General Laws or reduction under section 9C of 
said chapter 29 without express authorization from the general court. Notwithstanding section 19A of said 
chapter 29, any transfer under this section shall be made by the comptroller in accordance with a transfer 
schedule to be developed for each item by the comptroller after consulting with the appropriate agency 
secretary, the secretary of administration and finance and the state treasurer. The schedule for each 
appropriation shall provide for transfers in increments considered appropriate to meet the cash flow needs 
of each fund; provided, however, that the sum of the incremental transfers shall equal the sum set forth in 
this section and all transfers under the schedule shall be completed not later than June 30, 2024. Not later 
than 7 days after the schedules receive final approval by the comptroller, they shall be reported to the house 
and senate committees on ways and means.

SECTION 2F. 
 
SECTION 2F. The sums set forth in this section are hereby appropriated from the Education and 
Transportation Fund for the purposes and subject to the conditions specifi ed in this section and subject to 
the laws regulating the disbursement of public funds for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2024. All 
appropriations in this section shall not be subject to section 5D of chapter 29 of the General Laws.

SECTION 3. Notwithstanding any general or special law to the contrary, for the fiscal year ending June 30, 
2024 the distribution of unrestricted general government aid to cities and towns of the balance of the State Lottery 
and Gaming Fund, as paid from the General Fund in accordance with clause (c) of the second paragraph of section 
35 of chapter 10 of the General Laws, and additional funds from the General Fund and the Gaming Local Aid Fund, 
shall be $1,270,595,794 and shall be apportioned to cities and towns in accordance with this section. 
For fiscal year 2024 the total amounts to be distributed and paid to each city, town and regional school district 
from items 7061-0008 and 7061-0009 of section 2, shall be as se t forth in the following lists. If there is conflict 
between the language of this section and the distribution listed below, the distribution below shall control. The 
specified amounts distributed from said item 7061-0008 of said section 2 shall be deemed in full satisfaction of the 
amounts due under chapter 70 of the General Laws. 
For fiscal year 2024, a district’s school aid shall be calculated according to the provisions of said chapter 70. 
The foundation budget category of “low -income enrollment” for the purpose of calculating foundation enrollment 
shall be determined by financial eligibility for certain federal programs, as defined by the provisions of section 2 of 
said chapter 70, and including a number of students identified and approved as low income through the supplemental 
claiming system established and posted by the department for that purpose, as well as students identified and 
approved as homeless for purposes of calculating the McKinney -Vento homelessness grant program administered 
by the depar tment, consistent with the conditions provided for in said section 2 . The assumed special education 
enrollment percentage for vocational school students shall be set at 4.90 per cent and the assumed special education 
enrollment percentage for non-vocational school students shall be set at 3.90 per cent. 
The per -pupil rates for the employee benefits and fixed charges allotments shall be adjusted by the foundation 
employee benefits inflation rate and the per -pupil rates for all other foundation allotments sh all be adjusted by the foundation 
inflation index. Foundation increments shall be the additional resources provided for the education of students designated as 
English learners or low-income; provided, however, that for low-income students the amount of the foundation increment shall 
be determined by the low -income group into which each district is assigned. Foundation budget rates for employee benefits 
and fixed charges, guidance and psychological services, special education out -of-district tuition, Englis h learners and low -
income students shall be increased by three-sixths of the gap between the rates used in fiscal year 2021 and the rates 
established in tables 1 and 2 of section 3 of said chapter 70, consistent with adjustments prescribed in said section 3 
and set at the rates identified in the table below. Required local contributions shall be calculated pursuant to said chapter 
70; provided, that municipal revenue growth factors shall be calculated in a manner consistent with calculations 
made in fiscal year 2023; provided further, that the total statewide target local contribution shall be 59 percent and 
the effort reduction percentage shall be 100 percent; and provided further that the minimum aid per pupil dollar 
amount shall be $60. 
Chapter 70 aid for fiscal year 2024 shall be the greater of: (i) foundation aid, or (ii) the sum of base aid and 
minimum aid. No non -operating district shall receive chapter 70 aid in an amount greater than the district’s 
foundation budget. 
The department of elementary and secondary education shall not consider health care costs for retired 
teachers to be part of net school spending for any district in which such costs were not considered part of net school 
spending in fiscal year 1994 and for any district that has not accepted the provisions of section 260 of chapter 165 
of the acts of 2014; provided, however, that any district for wh om such costs are not so considered shall have 
 
 
included as part of net school spending an amount equal to the increase in the foundation budget for the district 
associated with health care costs of retired teachers. 
No payments to cities, towns or counties maintaining an agricultural school under this section shall be made 
after November 30 of the fiscal year until the commissioner of revenue certifies acceptance of the prior fiscal year’s 
annual financial reports submitted under section 43 of chapter 44 of the General Laws. Advance payments shall be 
made for some or all of periodic local reimbursement or assistance programs to any city, town, regional school 
district or independent agricultural school that demonstrates an emergency cash shortfall, as certi fied by the 
commissioner of revenue and approved by the secretary of administration and finance, under guidelines established 
by the secretary.

SECTION 6. Said chapter 6 is hereby further amended by adding the following section:- 12 
 
Section 222. (a) For the purposes of this section, “state agency” shall mean the executive 13 
and judicial branches of the government of the commonwealth, any special legislative 14 
commission created by the general court and any agency, department or quasi-state agency. 15 
 
(b) Notwithstanding any general or special law to the contrary, a state agency required by 16 
law to file reports with the general court or a committee thereof shall provide an electronic copy 17 
of the report to the clerks of the senate and house of representatives. The clerks of the senate and 18 
house of representatives shall: (i) make all such reports available online to the public in an 19 
accessible, searchable format through the general court’s website; and (ii) create and maintain an 20 
archive of all such reports that is available online in a searchable format. The clerks of the senate 21 
and house of representatives shall develop procedures and requirements for the preparation of 22 
such reports to facilitate their collection and storage. A state agency submitting a report shall 23 
notify, in writing, every entity that is required by law to receive the report of the availability of 24 
the report on the general court’s website and of the means of accessing the report. A state agency 25 
shall provide a hard copy of any such report upon request from an entity that is required by law 26 
to receive the report. Compliance with this section shall fulfill any general or special law 27 
requirement for the filing of a report by a state agency with the general court. 28 
 
SECTION 7. Chapter 6A of the General Laws is hereby amended by adding the 29 
following section:- 30 
 
Section 109. (a) For the purposes of this section, the following words shall, unless the 31 
context clearly requires otherwise, have the following meanings: 32 
 
“Government agency”, a legal entity of state government established by the general court 33 
or by executive order as an agency, board, bureau, commission, council, department, office or 34 
division within the executive branch of the commonwealth with a specific mission and which is 35 
subject to the control of the governor or a quasi-public entity. 36 
 
“Personal identifying information”, information: (i) that directly identifies an individual, 37 
 
 
including name, address, social security number or other identifying number or code; (ii) by 38 
which an agency intends to identify specific individuals in conjunction with other data elements, 39 
which shall include indirect identification that may compile an identity, such as a combination of 40 
gender, race, birth date, geographic indicator and other descriptors; or (iii) that permits the 41 
physical or online contacting of a specific individual. 42 
 
(b) Every government agency that collects demographic data as to the race or ethnicity of 43 
residents of the commonwealth shall use separate collection and tabulations for the following: 44 
 
(i) each major Asian group, as reported by the United States Census Bureau, including, 45 
but not limited to, Chinese, Japanese, Filipino, Korean, Vietnamese, Asian Indian, Laotian, 46 
Cambodian, Bangladeshi, Hmong, Indonesian, Malaysian, Pakistani, Sri Lankan, Taiwanese, 47 
Nepalese, Burmese, Tibetan and Thai; 48 
 
(ii) each major Pacific Islander group, as reported by the United States Census Bureau, 49 
including, but not limited to, Native Hawaiian, Guamanian, Samoan, Fijian and Tongan; 50 
 
(iii) each other Asian or Pacific Islander group not listed in clause (i) or (ii); 51 
 
(iv) each major Black or African American group, as reported by the United States 52 
Census Bureau, including, but not limited to, African American, Jamaican, Haitian, Nigerian, 53 
Ethiopian, Cape Verdean and Somali; 54 
 
(v) each major Latino group, as reported by the United States Census Bureau, including, 55 
but not limited to, Mexican, Puerto Rican, Cuban, Salvadoran, Dominican and Colombian; and 56 
 
(vi) each major white or Caucasian group, as reported by the United States Census 57 
Bureau, including, but not limited to, German, Irish, English, Italian, Polish, Portuguese and 58 
French. 59 
 
(c) Each government agency shall allow an individual to choose more than 1 group, write 60 
in their own group or choose the aggregate category. No government agency shall fill out racial 61 
or ethnic information unless directed by the individual or required by state or federal law to fill 62 
out such information on the individual’s behalf. 63 
 
(d) Except for personal identifying information, which shall be deemed confidential, each 64 
government agency shall make the data available to the public in accordance with state and 65 
federal law. Data may be maintained in paper, electronic or other media form. To prevent 66 
identification of individuals, the data may be aggregated into categories at a state, county, city, 67 
census tract or zip code level to facilitate comparisons, to identify disparities and to be included 68 
in studies and reports. This subsection shall not be construed to prevent any other government 69 
agency from posting data collected on the agency’s website in a manner prescribed in this 70 
section. 71 
 
(e)(1) The secretary of administration and finance shall establish regulations and 72 
guidelines on the collection of demographic data, which shall include, but not be limited to: (i) a 73 
 
 
standardized form for information collection; (ii) revising the categories of race and ethnicity to 74 
ensure continued alignment with the categories reported by the United States Census Bureau, as 75 
set forth in the federal Office of Management and Budget’s statistical standards for collecting 76 
and reporting race and ethnicity data across federal agencies; (iii) expanding the categories to 77 
ensure that individuals are able to accurately express self identification; (iv) a standardized 78 
format for agencies to make data publicly available and to update said data on an annual basis; 79 
(v) a method to ensure that no personal identifying information is publicly released; (vi) a 80 
standardized written disclosure to the individual completing the form that information collection 81 
is voluntary; (vii) procedures to ensure that nonparticipation in information collection shall have 82 
no impact on an individual’s eligibility for state services; (viii) an annual review of the cost 83 
impact and success of collecting information; and (ix) a process by which government agencies 84 
may apply to the secretary of administration and finance for a programmatic or partial waiver 85 
from the requirements of this section based upon: (A) contradictory obligations under state or 86 
federal law; (B) a demonstration that the information cannot be collected without imposing a 87 
burden that outweighs the benefits of collection; or (C) a demonstration that the information 88 
collected cannot be reported in a way that protects personal identifying information. 89 
 
(2) Annually, there shall be not less than 1 public hearing on the implementation of or 90 
changes in the regulations and guidelines established pursuant to paragraph (1). 91 
 
(3) Annually, not later than August 1, the secretary of administration and finance shall 92 
file a report on the progress of data collection to the clerks of the house of representatives and 93 
senate and the joint committee on state administration and regulatory oversight. Said report shall 94 
include a list of all waivers granted to government agency programs pursuant to paragraph (1) 95 
and the grounds upon which each waiver was granted. 96 
 
(f) All data collected by government agencies shall be subject to state and federal privacy 97 
laws, including, but not limited to, Title 13 of the United States Code and section 2 of chapter 98 
93H. 99 
 
SECTION 8. Chapter 6C of the General Laws is hereby amended by adding the 100 
following section:- 101 
 
Section 79. (a) For the purposes of this section, the following words shall, unless the 102 
context clearly requires otherwise, have the following meanings: 103 
 
“Aggregate”, granular materials such as gravel, sand and crushed rock that may be used 104 
individually or are combined for a particular purpose. 105 
 
“Certified professional geologist”, a professional geologist certified by the American 106 
Institute of Professional Geologists. 107 
 
“Concrete aggregate”, natural sand, natural gravel or crushed aggregate products 108 
produced from ledge rock. 109 
 
 
 
“Licensed professional geologist”, a professional geologist certified by: (i) examination 110 
through the National Association of State Boards of Geology; or (ii) a state’s licensing authority 111 
that follows the national standards of the National Association of State Boards of Geology’s 112 
licensing program or its equivalent. 113 
 
(b) Any person seeking to mine, expand, excavate or otherwise operate a quarry, sand 114 
and gravel operation or any other aggregate source for the purpose of producing concrete 115 
aggregate for sale or use in foundations, structural elements or infrastructure, including, but not 116 
limited to, roadways and bridges, shall submit to the department and the state geologist an 117 
application for a license to conduct such activity. 118 
 119 
Each license application shall consist of: (i) a description of the geographic location of 120 
the aggregate source; (ii) an operations plan, including, but not limited to, mining, processing, 121 
storage and quality control methods; (iii) a geological source report, consistent with subsection 122 
(c); and (iv) the results of aggregate testing for the presence of pyrite and pyrrhotite, consistent 123 
with subsection (d). Each license application shall be accompanied by a fee as established by the 124 
department. Fees received by the department under this section shall be used to implement this 125 
section; provided, however, that any surplus fee receipts shall be deposited into the General 126 
Fund. 127 
 128 
(c) An applicant under this section shall prepare a geological source report as required 129 
under subsection (b). Such report shall be prepared by a certified professional geologist, licensed 130 
professional geologist or an equivalent acceptable to the state geologist in a form and manner 131 
prescribed by the department, developed in consultation with the state geologist, a representative 132 
nominated by the Massachusetts Aggregate & Asphalt Pavement Association, Inc. and a 133 
representative nominated by the Massachusetts Concrete & Aggregate Producers Association, 134 
Inc., and shall include, but shall not be limited to: (i) a description of the characteristics of the 135 
aggregate to be excavated at the aggregate source location; (ii) a description of the products to be 136 
produced at such location; and (iii) a copy of the results of an inspection of face material and 137 
geologic log analysis, which shall be conducted not more than 60 days prior to the date of the 138 
report. A geological source report prepared under this subsection shall be valid for a period of 1 139 
year from the date of preparation. 140 
 141 
(d) Aggregate testing to identify the presence of pyrite and pyrrhotite required under 142 
subsection (b) shall include, but shall not be limited to, a total sulfur test to measure total sulfur 143 
content in a representative sample. Aggregate testing shall be performed by an accredited 144 
laboratory in accordance with applicable standards established by American Society of Testing 145 
and Materials International or alternate standards to be determined by the department in 146 
consultation with the state geologist. 147 
 148 
(e) The secretary or a designee, in consultation with the state geologist, shall review each 149 
license application submitted pursuant to this section and notify each applicant whether the 150 
license has been approved and any applicable conditions of operation. If the application is 151 
denied, the notification shall include the reason for denial. A license granted under this section 152 
shall be valid for 1 year from the date of approval; provided, however, that a license may be 153 
renewed after it expires. The department shall state the aggregate testing requirements 154 
 
 
established under subsection (d) in the license application; provided, however, that the state 155 
geologist may request additional testing or information during the review of a license 156 
application. The department may modify testing requirements and application criteria at its 157 
discretion. 158 
 159 
The department may issue a license valid for more than 1 year to an applicant that has 160 
submitted geological source reports and been approved for a license for 5 consecutive years; 161 
provided, however, that the licensee shall be required to submit annual geologic source reports as 162 
a condition for receiving such license. 163 
 164 
(f) A person owning or operating an aggregate source, subject to licensure pursuant to 165 
this section, shall maintain all records relevant to such licensure and operation, including, but not 166 
limited to, a record of sale for all aggregate, for not less than 30 years. 167 
 168 
(g) A person owning or operating a concrete production facility for the purpose of 169 
producing concrete for sale or use in foundations, structural elements or infrastructure, including, 170 
but not limited to, roadways and bridges, and who is in receipt of aggregate material from a 171 
source licensed pursuant to this section, shall maintain a record of the aggregate used in 172 
individual concrete batches for not less than 30 years. 173 
 174 
(h) The department, in consultation with the state geologist, shall maintain all data 175 
collected under this section. 176 
 177 
(i) Nothing in this section shall affect the operations of quarries producing aggregate for 178 
purposes other than those described in subsection (b). 179 
 180 
(j) The department, in consultation with the state geologist, shall promulgate regulations 181 
to implement this section. 182

SECTION 11. Section 9 of chapter 15A of the General Laws, as amended by section 43 197 
of chapter 7 of the acts of 2023, is hereby further amended by adding the following paragraph:- 198 
 199 
 
 
Notwithstanding any general or special law to the contrary, for the purpose of 200 
determining eligibility for in-state tuition rates and fees and for state-funded financial assistance 201 
at public institutions of higher education, any individual admitted to such public institutions of 202 
higher education, other than a nonimmigrant alien within the meaning of 8 U.S.C. § 203 
1101(a)(15)(A) to (S), inclusive, who attended high school in the commonwealth for not less 204 
than 3 years and graduated from a high school in the commonwealth or attained the equivalent 205

eligible on the same terms as other individuals for state-funded financial assistance at such state-207 
funded public and state-approved private, independent nonprofit institutions of higher education; 208 
provided, however, that any individual who is eligible for the military selective service under the 209 
federal Military Selective Service Act, as amended by 50 U.S.C. 14 App. 453 § 3, shall register 210 
for such. No individual qualified for in-state tuition rates and fees under this chapter shall be 211 
denied in-state tuition and fees as a result of the granting of eligibility under this paragraph. To 212 
receive in-state tuition under this section, an eligible individual shall provide the public 213 
institution of higher education where the eligible individual is or plans to become enrolled with a 214 
high school transcript or certificate demonstrating completion of the equivalent thereof in the 215 
commonwealth and: (i) a valid social security number; (ii) a document reflecting issuance of an 216 
individual taxpayer identification number; (iii) if that individual is not a citizen of the United 217 
States or a legal permanent resident of the United States, an affidavit signed under the pains and 218 
penalties of perjury stating that the individual has applied for citizenship or legal permanent 219 
residence or will apply for citizenship or legal permanent residence in accordance with federal 220 
statute and federal regulations within 120 days of eligibility for such status; or (iv) 221 
documentation of registration with the selective service, if applicable. 222

SECTION 12. Said chapter 15A is hereby further amended by inserting after section 16 224 
the following section:- 225 
 226 
Section 16A. (a) There shall be a scholarship program, subject to appropriation, to be 227 
administered by the board, which shall be known as the high demand targeted scholarship 228 
program, to provide financial assistance to students in the commonwealth who are enrolled in 229 
and pursuing a program of higher education for an in-demand profession as defined by the 230 
executive office of labor and workforce development’s study on labor market conditions. 231 
 232 
(b)(1) Eligibility for the scholarship program shall be limited to students that: (i) reside in 233 
the commonwealth for at least 1 year prior to the start of the academic year; (ii) agree to 234 
complete an undergraduate or graduate degree or certificate program at a public institution of 235 
higher education pursuant to section 5; (iii) maintain a minimum grade point average of 3.0 236 
annually and demonstrate satisfactory academic progress in accordance with institutional 237 
standards; (iv) successfully complete an undergraduate or graduate degree or certificate program 238 
at said public institution of higher education; (v) enter into an in-demand occupation, as defined 239 
by the executive office of labor and workforce development’s study on labor market conditions, 240 
in the commonwealth; provided, that said in-demand occupation shall be consistent with the 241 
undergraduate or graduate degree or certificate; (vi) commit to working in the commonwealth for 242 
a term of not less than 5 years in an in-demand occupation as defined by said study; and (vii) 243 
meet any additional criteria required by the board. 244 
 245 
 
 
(2) Scholarships shall be awarded to qualified students to cover the cost of tuition, fees 246 
and additional costs of attendance as calculated by the student’s public institution of higher 247 
education, including, but not limited to, room and board, books and supplies, transportation, 248 
child care and personal expenses associated with obtaining an undergraduate or graduate degree 249 
or certificate program at a public institution of higher education. 250 
 251 
(c) The board, in coordination with the Massachusetts state scholarship office, shall: 252 
 253 
(1) promulgate guidelines governing the high demand targeted scholarship program; 254 
 255 
(2) promulgate procedures for repayment of the amount of scholarship benefits for 256 
persons who participate in the program but who fail to complete the 5-year commitment pursuant 257 
to clause (vi) of paragraph (1) of subsection (b); provided, however, that the procedures shall be 258 
designed to ensure there are no disincentives for low-income students to participate in the 259 
program and shall consider: (i) the amount of scholarship benefits the participant has received; 260 
(ii) the participant’s current income if not working in an in-demand occupation; and (iii) the 261 
amount of time the participant worked in the commonwealth in the in-demand occupation 262 
consistent with their undergraduate or graduate degree or certificate; and 263 
 264 
(3) establish an outreach plan to attract individuals to in-demand professions through the 265 
scholarship program. 266 
 267 
(d) Annually, not later than July 31, the board shall submit a report detailing activity of 268 
the program, including, but not limited to: (i) the number of scholarships awarded by the 269 
program; provided, that the board shall categorize the number of scholarship awards by in-270 
demand profession and public institution of higher education; (ii) demographic information of 271 
the recipients of the scholarship program; and (iii) the average scholarship award amount, which 272 
shall be categorized by in-demand profession and public institution of higher education. 273 
 274

SECTION 43. Chapter 111 of the General Laws is hereby amended by inserting after 843 
section 24N the following section:- 844 
 845 
Section 24O. (a) As used in this section, the following words shall, unless the context 846 
clearly requires otherwise, have the following meanings: 847 
 848 
“Maternal morbidity”, any health condition attributed to or aggravated by pregnancy that 849 
has negative health outcomes. 850 
 851 
“Maternal mortality”, the death of an individual, from any cause, during pregnancy or 852 
within 1 year of the end of the pregnancy, regardless of the duration and site of the pregnancy. 853 
 854 
(b)(i) There shall be within the department a maternal mortality and morbidity review 855 
committee to review maternal mortality, study the incidence of pregnancy complications and 856 
maternal morbidity and make recommendations to improve maternal outcomes and eliminate 857 
preventable maternal deaths. 858 
 859 
(ii) The committee shall access relevant records and reports pertaining to incidents of 860 
maternal mortality or near-death cases under its review. All relevant records and reports shall 861 
remain in the possession of committee staff and only de-identified information shall be presented 862 
or otherwise shared. 863 
 864 
(c) The committee shall: 865 
 866 
(i) conduct case reviews of maternal mortality and maternal morbidity in the 867 
commonwealth; 868 
 869 
(ii) make recommendations to improve access to high-quality, evidence-based health care 870 
for pregnant individuals and infants in the commonwealth; 871 
 872 
(iii) identify gaps in the provision of health care services for pregnant individuals who 873 
experience maternal mortality or maternal morbidity, including, but not limited to, disparities in 874 
access to: quality care; appropriate health care; transportation; and financial resources. The 875 
committee shall identify such gaps by analyzing the pregnant individuals’: 876 
 877 
(1) race, ethnicity and age; 878 
 879 
(2) geographic region of residence; and 880 
 881 
(3) socioeconomic status; 882 
 883 
(iv) review probable cause of death and identify contributing factors in cases reviewed 884 
pursuant to clause (i), to the extent possible; 885 
 886 
(v) determine, to the extent possible, whether the death or health condition presented in 887 
cases reviewed pursuant to clause (i) was preventable, and if so, what actions could have been 888 
 
 
taken to prevent the death or health condition; and 889 
 890 
(vi) make recommendations to prevent maternal mortality and maternal morbidity and to 891 
eliminate disparities in maternal health outcomes. 892 
 893 
(d)(1) The committee shall maintain all information, documents and records in possession 894 
of the committee as confidential and not subject to subpoena or discovery in any civil or criminal 895 
proceeding; provided, however, that information, documents and records otherwise available 896 
from other sources shall not be exempt from subpoena or discovery solely because such 897 
information, documents and records were presented to or reviewed by the committee. 898 
 899 
(2) A physician, hospital or pharmacy providing the committee access to medical records 900 
pursuant to this section shall not be liable for civil damages or be subject to any criminal or 901 
disciplinary action for good faith efforts in providing such records. 902 
 903 
(3) Information, records, reports, statements, notes, memoranda or other data collected 904 
pursuant to this section shall not be otherwise admissible as evidence in any action before a court 905 
or any other tribunal, board or agency. Such information, records, reports, statements, notes, 906 
memoranda or other data shall not be exhibited, and their contents shall not be disclosed in any 907 
way, in whole or in part, by any officer or representative of the department or any other person, 908 
except as may be necessary to further the review of the committee and as may be allowed by this 909 
section. No person participating in such review shall disclose, in any manner, the information so 910 
obtained except in conformity with review of the committee. 911 
 912 
(4) All proceedings and activities of the committee and records obtained, created or 913 
maintained pursuant to this section, including records of interviews, written reports and 914 
statements procured by the department or any other person, agency or organization acting jointly 915 
or under contract with the department in connection with this section shall be confidential. 916 
 917 
(5) Members of the committee and staff members of the committee shall not be subject to 918 
questioning in any civil or criminal proceeding regarding ongoing or completed reviews of the 919 
committee; provided, however, that nothing in this section shall be construed to prevent a 920 
member of the committee from testifying to information obtained independently of the 921 
proceedings of the committee or which is public information. 922 
 923 
(d)(1) The committee shall consist of the following members: the commissioner, or their 924 
designee, who shall serve as chair; a representative of the department of public health; a 925 
representative of the Perinatal-Neonatal Quality Improvement Network of Massachusetts; the 926 
chief medical examiner, or their designee; the chair of the Massachusetts chapter of the 927

health professional; a representative from academia in a relevant field; a medical professional 935

 942

SECTION 90. Notwithstanding any general or special law to the contrary and not later 1669 
 
 
than 180 days after the effective date of this act, the department of public health shall promulgate 1670 
regulations that create: (i) a statewide standard pre-hospital care protocol related to the 1671 
assessment, treatment and transport of stroke patients by emergency medical services providers 1672 
to a hospital designated by the department to care for stroke patients; provided, however, that the 1673 
protocol shall be based on national evidence-based guidelines for transport of stroke patients, 1674 
consider transport that crosses state lines and include plans for the triage and transport of 1675 
suspected stroke patients, including, but not limited to, those who may have an emergent large 1676 
vessel occlusion, to an appropriate facility within a specified timeframe following the onset of 1677 
symptoms and additional criteria to determine which level of care is the most appropriate 1678 
destination; (ii) statewide criteria for designating hospitals in a tiered system, featuring advanced 1679 
designations in addition to primary stroke services, to treat stroke patients based on patient 1680 
acuity; provided, however, that the tiers shall be based on criteria from at least 1 nationally-1681 
recognized program and shall not permit self-designation; provided further, that in developing 1682 
such criteria, the department shall consider: (a) designation models and criteria developed by the 1683 
Joint Commission, DNV GL Healthcare USA, Inc. or another national certifying body 1684 
recognized by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services; (b) designation models and 1685 
criteria adopted by other states and the differences in geography and health care resources of 1686 
such other states; (c) the clinical and operational capability of a facility to provide stroke 1687 
services, including emergency and ancillary stroke services; (d) limiting the routing of stroke 1688 
patients to thrombectomy-capable facilities whenever a comprehensive stroke center is within a 1689 
recommended timeframe to maximize technical competency and patient outcomes; and (e) 1690 
procedures to suspend or revoke a facility’s designation if the department determines that the 1691 
facility is not in compliance with designation requirements and procedures to notify emergency 1692 
medical services providers of any such suspension or revocation; and (iii) recommended national 1693 
evidence-based quality and utilization measure sets for stroke care for use by the center for 1694 
health information and analysis pursuant to section 14 of chapter 12C of the General Laws; 1695 
provided, however, that the department shall consider measures in current use in national quality 1696 
improvement programs, including, but not limited to, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid 1697 
Services, the National Quality Forum, the Paul Coverdell National Acute Stroke Program or 1698 
other nationally recognized data platforms. 1699
